text:
elena: FYI — received P1 from a customer. They say our Python SDK in JSON/stream mode is dropping nested "meta" objects intermittently which yields invalid JSON on their downstream parser. Raising to eng.

mike: ugh. any repro or sample payloads? which sdk version?

elena: customer reported v1.12.0. Attached their logs (redacted). Snippet: 
```
RAW CHUNK RECEIVED:
{"id":"req-123","data":"...","meta":{"user":"u-42","prefs":{"t":true}}

NEXT CHUNK:
"more":"..."}
```
Resulting concatenation ends up: 
```
{"id":"req-123","data":"...","meta":{"user":"u-42","prefs":{"t":true}}
"more":"..."}
```
Which hits their strict json.loads -> JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter or '}' at line 1 column 78

tara: do we have a streaming reassembly test for nested objects? I know we added heartbeat splitting tests but not nested-object boundaries.

mike: also flagged: we changed the chunk-buffer logic in v1.12.0 to reduce copies (PR #489). Could be a buffer-truncation bug for deep nest boundaries.

elena: customer included a minimal repro script. I pasted it below (redacted to remove credentials):
```python
# repro_stream_drop.py
from redwood import StreamingClient
cli = StreamingClient(api_key="REDACTED")
with cli.stream(mode="json") as s:
    s.send({"id":1, "meta": {"a": {"b": {"c": 1}}}})
    # consumer on other side uses a strict newline-concat parser
```
They say after ~1000 messages the consumer fails intermittently.

ops-bot: ticket created: SUP-2026, priority P1, customer reporting production impact.

tara: I can try to reproduce locally with a fuzz harness that simulates random chunk splits at nested braces. Will run against v1.12.0 and main.

mike: please also log raw recv buffer boundaries in the client and assert that after reassembly the bytes form valid JSON before handing off to the serializer. If reassembly mutates bytes, great clue.

elena: customer offered to run a debug build but asked if we have a hotfix the can deploy quickly.

tara: timeline: Ill have initial repro within 2 hours. If repro is deterministic, we prepare a 1.12.1 patch that reverts the small-copy optimization. If intermittent and only in high-throughput, might need a more surgical fix.

mike: also add a unit test that streams fragments exactly at positions where nested object starts/ends. Add CI job that runs the fuzz harness for 60s.

elena: thanks. Ill update the customer and request their minimal reproducer plus sample consumer parser code and the OS/py version. They reported CPython 3.11 on linux.

tara: reproduced locally after ~30k iterations with fuzz harness. Confirmed reassembly omitted a single '\n' between chunks and that our chunk-join path had a branch where we drop leading newline when previous chunk ends with '}}'. Investigating now.

mike: great catch. likely edge-case in joiner that trims whitespace to optimize. That trimming should never touch structural characters.

tara: workaround to propose to customer: upgrade their consumer to a tolerant newline-agnostic concat OR pin SDK to v1.11.x. I'll craft a minimal patch and tests.

elena: customer prefers patch from us. Marking for fast-track.

ops-bot: deploy request SUP-2026-hotfix created, reviewer=lead-sdk, priority=high.

mike: once patch ready, run canary on internal infra for a day then push release tag and notify support for staged rollout. Also add postmortem checklist: root cause, missing test coverage, release note, customer compensation if SLA hit.

elena: noted. Will keep thread updates here. :thumbsup:
